title: H 4207 (118th General Assembly): Authorize A Person To Vote By Absentee Ballot If He Or A Parent Last Resided In This State Immediately Before His Or His Parent's Departure From The United States.

(section) SECTION 1 (amends 7-5-120, new subsection (C), as the Judiciary Committee amendment of 2/4/2010 rewrites it)
(quote) If a United States citizen outside the United States who has never lived in the United States has a parent who is a qualified elector, then that person is eligible to register and vote where the person's parent is a qualified elector; provided the person is not registered to vote in any other state or territory of the United States.
(section) SECTION 2 (amends 7-15-110(5)(a))
(quote) if a citizen or his parent last resided in South Carolina immediately before his or his parent's departure from the United States;
(other) SECTION 2 (7-15-110): adjusts the list of overseas and military persons who may register using the federal Standard Form 76 (plural wording, parent-residence rule for citizens living abroad).
(other) SECTION 3: takes effect upon approval by the Governor.
(other) version: latest-2010_bill-page is the only saved text and it holds the whole history page: the Judiciary Committee report of 2/4/2010 (corrected 2/5/2010 for a scrivener's error) followed by the bill text as introduced. The introduced text gives subsection (C) with no proviso; the committee amendment replaces (C) and adds 'provided the person is not registered to vote in any other state or territory'. Separate files for the 11/17/2009 and 2/4/2010 versions are not saved. No slot a-d text in any version.
(other) note: Slot e quotes the committee-amended (C) (the furthest version; the bill was recommitted on 2/17/2010 and went no further). The introduced version of (C), still printed in the file, lacks the proviso. The 7-5-120 reprint keeps the existing 'Every citizen of this State and the United States' language unchanged. Title mentions absentee ballots but the text amends 7-15-110 on registering with the federal form. No voter ID or proof-of-citizenship document rule.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
